translationRepairs: In the first month of Hailing's Zhenglong 4 (1159), the court closed the markets at Fengxiang Prefecture and at Tang, Deng, Ying, Cai, Gong, Tao, and Jiaoxi County, concentrating border trade at Sizhou alone.

In the first month of Hailing's Zhenglong 4 (1159), the court closed the markets at Fengxiang Prefecture and at Tang, Deng, Ying, Cai, Gong, Tao, and other prefectures, as well as Jiaoxi County, concentrating border trade at Sizhou alone.
s0005 has 唐、鄧、潁、蔡、鞏、洮等州並膠西縣; the idiomatic drops 等 and collapses the prefecture list into Jiaoxi County. Restoring "and other prefectures, as well as Jiaoxi County" matches the Chinese.
In the tenth month of Xuanzong's Zhenyou 3 (1215) Gao Rulü was sent to buy grain in Henan and require transport to the capital; capital granaries were also to buy any surplus the people still held.
In the tenth month of Xuanzong's Zhenyou 3 (1215) Gao Ruli was sent to buy grain in Henan and require transport to the capital; capital granaries were also to buy any surplus the people still held.
s0097 and s0098 name the same person 高汝礪; 礪 is lì, and s0098 already has Gao Ruli. Idiomatic Gao Rulü is a wrong romanization, not a distinct alias.

In the first month of year five an edict ordered plot farming; memorialist Wu Zhi Gao Yi had earlier submitted the method and asked to set planting quotas based on household registers and land holdings.

In the first month of year five an edict ordered plot farming; memorialist Gao Yi of Wuzhi had earlier submitted the method and asked to set planting quotas based on household registers and land holdings.
s0204 has 陳言人武陟高翌: 武陟 is the place Wuzhi and 高翌 is the personal name Gao Yi. Treating "Wu Zhi Gao Yi" as a fused personal name is wrong; "Gao Yi of Wuzhi" is accurate.

In the first month of the fifth year an edict instructed farmers to use plot farming; earlier, memorialist Wu Zhi Gao Yi submitted the plot-farming method and also requested verifying household registers and land holdings, fixing quotas for planting.

In the first month of the fifth year an edict instructed farmers to use plot farming; earlier, memorialist Gao Yi of Wuzhi submitted the plot-farming method and also requested verifying household registers and land holdings, fixing quotas for planting.
Same source phrase 武陟高翌 on the literal field: Wuzhi is the place qualifier, Gao Yi the name. The proposed "Gao Yi of Wuzhi" corrects the fusion.

The original three-month-per-capita target risked spoilage and was replaced by tiered quotas: 30,000 shi for counties above 20,000 households, 20,000 for above 10,000, 15,000 for 5,000–10,000, and 5,000 for below 5,000.

The original plan to store three months' grain by household register risked spoilage from large quantities and was replaced by tiered quotas: 30,000 shi for counties above 20,000 households, 20,000 for above 10,000, 15,000 for 5,000–10,000, and 5,000 for below 5,000.

s0148 舊擬備戶口三月之糧，恐數多致損 is not well rendered by "three-month-per-capita target risked spoilage"; restore household-register storage and spoilage from large quantities. But surrounding units fix county granaries, so keep "counties" rather than the proposal's vaguer "places".
Officials who induced 5,000 shi or more had one review grade reduced; 10,000 shi brought one promotion and two grades reduced; 20,000 shi one promotion and one grade raised—all to current vacancies.

Investigation and county officials who induced 5,000 shi or more had one review grade reduced; 10,000 shi brought one promotion and two grades reduced; 20,000 shi one promotion and one grade raised—all to current vacancies.
s0232 specifies 司縣官, and s0231 already renders the same office class as "Investigation and county officials"; bare "Officials" drops that qualification.

In Xuanzong's Zhenyou 2, on Daxing Prefecture Administrator Xu Ding's request, provisional favor-sale rates were fixed for rank advancement, mourning candidates seeking office, manumission of registered households, and similar benefits, each with set grain or fodder payments.

In Xuanzong's Zhenyou 2, on Daxing Prefecture Administrator Xu Ding's request, provisional favor-sale rates were fixed for advancement in palace rank and promotion, permission for those in mourning to take examinations and seek office, manumission of registered households, and similar benefits, each with set grain or fodder payments.
s0226 lists 進宮升職 and 丁憂人許應舉求仕; "rank advancement" and "mourning candidates seeking office" omit palace-rank/promotion pairing and the explicit permission to sit examinations (應舉).
